description:
Elixir allows `in` with a literal list or range in a guard (`when x in [false, nil]`, `when x in 1..3`); Elixir's own Kernel uses it. fz rewrites `in` to a call to `Enum.member?` (source_sugar.rs:137), which a guard refuses: "compiler2 case/with guards must be dispatch-pure" (jobs/body.rs:786), and the same for entry guards.

Expected: in a guard, `x in [a, b]` with a literal list is `x === a or x === b`, and `x in first..last//step` with literal bounds is the integer range test, as Elixir expands them; outside guards `in` stays Enumerable membership. Checked against Elixir on interp, run and build. Not needed by the distiller.
title: in with a literal list or range is allowed in a guard, as in Elixir
